title: Permission denied (publickey): How to Fix SSH Key Rejection
linkedin:
> Run `ssh -vvv user@host` first.

The verbose log shows exactly which keys your client offered and how the server answered, which is the whole diagnosis. From there it's usually one of five things: the right key isn't loaded, the public key isn't in the server's `authorized_keys`, permissions on `~/.ssh` are too loose, you're using the wrong username, or the key type is disabled.

Read the full guide: https://www.kloudbean.com/blog/fix-permission-denied-publickey/
